sources.citation: Paschen, Ludger, Susanne Fuchs & Frank Seifart. 2022. Final lengthening and vowel length in 25 languages. Journal of Phonetics 94: 101179 (HAL hal-04851145). Appendix A 'Phonological profiles', Fanbyak entry, article p.17.
sources.note: Explicitly: 'Fanbyak is still a largely underdescribed language, especially with regards to its prosody, so little can be said about tone, stress, or accent.' Gives 7-vowel inventory with length, (C)V(C) syllables; instrumental result: across-the-board phrase-final lengthening of vowels in both final and penultimate syllables (pp.9, 14) -- a boundary effect, not a stress claim.

sources.citation: Franjieh, Michael J. 2012. Possessive classifiers in North Ambrym, a language of Vanuatu: explorations in semantic classification. PhD thesis, SOAS, University of London. 406 pp. Sec. 1.1.2 'The Languages of Ambrym' p.18 and sec. 2.1 'Dialect variation' p.39 on Orkon/Fanbak.

The only stress statement in the thesis (p.55) concerns North Ambrym: 'Stress is not lexically contrastive and appears to be weight sensitive. Stress appears on syllables that have a coda.. When all syllables of a root are either light or heavy, stress falls on the penultimate syllable' -- another languoid (nort2839).

sources.citation: Rangelov, Tihomir, Eleanor Ridge & Lana Takau. 2025. Linguistics in Vanuatu 45 years after Independence. Te Reo: the Journal of the Linguistic Society of New Zealand 68(2) (Special Issue: Vanuatu languages in context): 31-78. Appendix 'Summary Table', row 89 (Ambrym-Paama region): Orkon-Fanbak orko1234.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content. State-of-documentation survey of 118 Vanuatu languages; the appendix summary table (p.49) codes Orkon-Fanbak orko1234 as Grammar = 'No grammar', Lexicon = 'Short list', Research score 1.0, Annotated corpus = 'Interlinear' (Franjieh's ELAR/DoReCo corpus), Bible = 'No Bible'. Body text mentions Franjieh's northern Ambrym corpus (DELAMAN award 2019) and dictionaries for all but one Ambrym language, but gives no linguistic description of Fanbyak. Confirms, as of Dec 2025 and by Vanuatu specialists, that no grammar or sketch of Fanbyak/Orkon exists.

sources.note: Nothing linguistic. The abstract reads: 'A documentation and description of the highly endangered language of Orkon/Fanbak. With around 30 active speakers of varying fluency, Orkon/Fanbak was originally spoken in the two villages of Orkon and Fanbak.. and comprised of two dialects.. The documentation consists of a grammar sketch, a corpus of texts from different speech genres, and a detailed sociolinguistic study of social networks and language shift/loss'. sources.citation: Lynch, John (data entry; source given as 'Crowley, Lynch, Early - notes'). 2007 [updated 2016]. Orkon. Language 476 in Greenhill, Simon J., Robert Blust & Russell D. Gray (eds.), Austronesian Basic Vocabulary Database. 192-item wordlist with notes ('A moribund language of West Ambrym, Vanuatu..'; 'No final phonemic analysis of the vowels has been done, due to inadequate data').
sources.note: No phonology prose beyond the 'problems' note that mid-vowel quality (e vs open e, o vs open o) was never phonemically resolved; the 192 forms are in broad phonetic transcription with vowel length (macrons/double vowels), labialised consonants and morpheme bars, but carry no stress, accent or pitch marks -- wordlist-only data, no statement on stress or tone.
